thread:
meera: Heads up — saw a 3x tail-latency spike on a few small LLM endpoints during GPU downscale last night. Digging in now.

meera: Snapshot: us-west1a, autoscaler removed 2 warm nodes while pods were finishing checkpoint/kvcache flush. Model load for that variant is ~45s cold.

tom: Oof. Is this the warm-pool eviction timing again or something different? Any logs from kubelet / drain?

meera: Logs show `PreStop` finished but KV upload lagged because we throttled IO; drain completed and pod was rescheduled -> hit model load. Warm-pool evictions happened at ~03:12 UTC.

rachel: Sounds like we should try a tiered-idle approach rather than binary warm vs cold. Hot = always-on for high QPS, Warm = snooze (fast resume), Cold = scale-to-zero. Snooze window might avoid these edge coldstarts.

jason: +1. Concrete: increase drain grace to 120s, add `snoozeWindow: 10m` for warm nodes, and prewarm trigger when pending queue > 2 or avg wait > 250ms.

sam: Cost/benefit check — hot GPU ~= $2.40/hr, warm (partial) ~= $0.65/hr if we keep memory & minimal power; warm+10% across fleet projected +$1.6k/month but reduces coldstart 99p latency ~30%. Worth running canary.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: applied patch redwood/infra#872: added `snoozeWindow` field to nodepool CR for canary cluster.

meera: Also add AZ affinity for warm nodes. We hit AZ-exhaustion once when prewarmed nodes were spread and pods then got scheduled in exhausted AZ. Keep prewarmed nodes local to the shard's AZ.

tom: Putting a sample cluster-autoscaler tuning snippet here for reference:
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-unready-time=20m
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
--max-graceful-termination-sec=120
```
These were our prior flags, backoff might need to be relaxed for warm pools.

jason: We should also emit metrics for `kvcache_persist_latency_ms` and `model_load_seconds` tagged by `model_variant` and `seq_len_bucket`. That will allow automated decisions on whether a warm node is worthwhile per workload.

rachel: I'll add a perf eval to sample 5% of traffic and track coldstart-success-rate. If coldstart errors or >5% tail errors, route traffic to hot route automatically.

sam: FYI finance: projected delta for +10% warm capacity in us-west = +$1.6k/mo, but expected savings from fewer SLO violations (support + infra ops) > $3k/mo historically.

meera: Plan: canary roll in us-west1a tonight — warm pool +10%, `snoozeWindow: 10m`, `drainGrace: 120s`, AZ affinity enforced. Monitor for 48h. If metrics look good, promote week-long rollout.

tom: SGTM. Oncall: please add alerts for `pod_scheduling_pending > 5` and `node_eviction_rate` spike. Also annotate the rollout in #eng-oncall.

rachel: I'll update the runbook with troubleshooting steps for KV flush failures and how to force a prewarm via the autoscaler API. Example CLI to trigger prewarm:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  https://infra.api.redwood/v1/nodepools/us-west1a/prewarm 
  -d '{"count":2, "pool":"warm"}'
```

meera: Thanks — I'll own the canary and post results. If things still break we'll try extending snoozeWindow to 30m or introduce a tiny burst capacity that never fully scales to zero.

sam: :thumbsup: Keep cost telemetry live. If we see unexpected +peak, pause rollout.

infra-bot: incident-bot: note created: #INF-5347 (canary warm-pool rollout)

meera: Closing loop — will post 12h and 48h snapshots. Thanks all.
